**Description**

<!--
Briefly describe the problem you are having in a few paragraphs.
-->

We observed the test was flaky in recent T2 testing with DNX chassis. Test injects 1000 identical packets, and expects them to be dropped.  But it failed in tx cnt check https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/34ce7e3c2cec20a7619af5b005dea21282bed8ef/tests/ip/test_ip_packet.py#L386-L387

PKT_NUM_ZERO is 100 in this case https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/34ce7e3c2cec20a7619af5b005dea21282bed8ef/tests/ip/test_ip_packet.py#L29

When test failed,  the value of `tx_ok` was something between 100 and 200. The `tx_ok` is likely counting the background traffic.  So it seems the computation of  `PKT_NUM_ZERO` is not quite working in T2 testing.

Furthermore, the tests also validates that expected packet should not egress out from switch. So not sure the above tx cnt check is really needed.
https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/34ce7e3c2cec20a7619af5b005dea21282bed8ef/tests/ip/test_ip_packet.py#L390-L391

comments.author: arista-nwolfe
comments.body:
This issue is hitting again on 202405 T2 devices, specifically on the upstream LCs it seems.

Here is an example of the number of packets seen on our recent runs:
```
cmp235-3:
Failed: Forwarded 276 packets in tx, not in expected range

cmp227-4:
Failed: Forwarded 275 packets in tx, not in expected range
Failed: Forwarded 264 packets in tx, not in expected range
Failed: Forwarded 295 packets in tx, not in expected range
Failed: Forwarded 316 packets in tx, not in expected range

cmp206-4:
Failed: Forwarded 301 packets in tx, not in expected range
Failed: Forwarded 264 packets in tx, not in expected range
```

I think maybe we should increase the tolerance from 20% to 40%.
I checked the device and all 1000 packets were RX_DROP'd on the ingress port so these TX_OK packets are all bgp and control traffic:
```
root@cmp235-3:~# show interfaces counters
Last cached time was 2024-12-10T22:16:35.704269
      IFACE    STATE    RX_OK      RX_BPS    RX_UTIL    RX_ERR    RX_DRP
-----------  -------  -------  ----------  ---------  --------  --------
Ethernet144        U   15,399  141.74 B/s      0.00%         0     1,000
```

linkedPullRequests.title: `ip/test_ip_packet.py` Increase `tx_ok` tolerance from `200` to `400` on T2
linkedPullRequests.author: arista-nwolfe
linkedPullRequests.body:
https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/issues/7954 described an issue we saw on T2 platforms where `test_ip_packet.py::test_forward_ip_packet_with_0xffff_chksum_drop` would fail sporadically if sufficient control/background traffic egressed the `out_ifaces`.

https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/8414 was created to fix this by increasing the tolerance from `100` to `200` packets. However, it seems like this wasn't sufficient tolerance as we're seeing failures on T2 devices:
```
Failed: Forwarded 276 packets in tx, not in expected range
Failed: Forwarded 275 packets in tx, not in expected range
Failed: Forwarded 264 packets in tx, not in expected range
Failed: Forwarded 295 packets in tx, not in expected range
Failed: Forwarded 316 packets in tx, not in expected range
Failed: Forwarded 301 packets in tx, not in expected range
Failed: Forwarded 264 packets in tx, not in expected range
```

But if we look at the RX_DROP counters we see all 1000 packets were dropped on RX:
```
root@cmp235-3:~# show interfaces counters
Last cached time was 2024-12-10T22:16:35.704269
      IFACE    STATE    RX_OK      RX_BPS    RX_UTIL    RX_ERR    RX_DRP
-----------  -------  -------  ----------  ---------  --------  --------
Ethernet144        U   15,399  141.74 B/s      0.00%         0     1,000
```

So the packets captured on TX was background traffic.

Summary:
Fixes #7954

comments.author: wenyiz2021
comments.body:
I'm ok with this change, but have a dumb question:

is it enough if we make sure Rx_drop is 1000? 
e.g. if Rx_drop is 1000, we can skip the range asserts because no packets are egress-ed and it's the most ideal case. if it is not exact match, we can check the range with tolerance?

comments.author: arista-nwolfe
comments.body:
> I'm ok with this change, but have a dumb question:
> 
> is it enough if we make sure Rx_drop is 1000? e.g. if Rx_drop is 1000, we can skip the range asserts because no packets are egress-ed and it's the most ideal case. if it is not exact match, we can check the range with tolerance?

Yeah IMO the TX_OK check seems like a weird one in this test, we should just check that all the packets were dropped on RX and that should be sufficient to indicate a passing test. But I'm not sure if certain platforms were failing because not all packets were being dropped or counted hence the tolerance was introduced? I figured rewriting the test to just check `RX_DROP` might cause issues on other platforms.
